assessment_summary: I validated the environment against both the guide and the installation summary, preferring behavioral evidence over file existence. (1) Toolchain: Ruby 3.1.4p223 and Node v20.11.0 exactly match the repo pins; PostgreSQL 14.24 is online; CMake, pkg-config, ImageMagick, shared-mime-info, memcached all present. (2) Dependencies: bundle check satisfied (311+ gems) and 419 npm packages. (3) Databases: all three exist with 262 tables each; the production DB has the guide's extensions in a shared_extensions schema plus the required database-level search_path. (4) Configuration: database.yml, secrets.yml (real generated secret_key_base, force_ssl: true, server_name localhost) and secret_emails.yml are present and consistent with the guide. (5) Behavioral verification: the development Rails server (left running on :3000) serves public pages with HTTP 200; I performed a genuine HTTP login as admin@consul.dev with the documented password using the form's actual field (user[login]) — 302 on POST, then the /admin backend, /admin/projekts, /admin/users and /admin/settings all return 200; mod@consul.dev also logs in. I independently BCrypt-verified all six documented seed accounts against Aa12345678. (6) Production setup: I independently booted RAILS_ENV=production bin/rails s on :3001 with its own pidfile — clean startup using the 211 precompiled assets, and force_ssl: true produced the documented 301→https redirect (TLS infeasible in-container without a public domain). The production DB is seeded (admin, 237 settings, 1 projekt) and the whenever crontab is installed; memcached answers VERSION 1.6.14. I stopped my transient production instance afterward, leaving the environment as found. (7) Test env: bin/rspec executes (e.g. spec/models/setting_spec.rb, spec/models/signature_spec.rb) against consul_test; failures are assertion-level. Limitations, all verified as environmental or pre-existing rather than installer faults: db:dev_seed aborts at the Debates section because committed seeds on this branch still pass the removed 'projekt' attribute while models were refactored to projekt_phase (git show HEAD confirms the committed code has the same stale references; no seed creates ProjektPhases) — the install summary's attribution is accurate and fixing it requires re-authoring application seed code, outside installation scope. Consequently the dev DB has demo projekts/users/settings but 0 debates/proposals, and factory-dependent specs fail. The guide's production steps 8–11 (Nginx, Let's Encrypt, Capistrano, systemd Puma/DelayedJob units) cannot be realized in this systemd-less container without a public domain; every app-level production step that is feasible in-container was completed and verified. SMTP is unconfigured, which the guide itself permits as a starting state since mail is queue-based. Overall, the software is demonstrably installed, complete within the environment's feasible scope, and operational, so I assessed success with these documented limitations.
